CONFIDENTIAL SEPARATION AGREEMENT AND GENERAL RELEASE

This Confidential Separation Agreement and General Release (this "Agreement") is between Halbrook Diagnostics, Inc. (the "Company") and Rosalind Achebe Kwan (the "Employee"), who is 58 years old.

1. SEPARATION DATE. The Employee's employment ends on April 30, 2026 (the "Separation Date"). The Employee will be paid all wages earned and all accrued unused vacation through that date, on that date, whether or not the Employee signs this Agreement, as California Labor Code §§ 201 and 227.3 require.

2. SEVERANCE. In exchange for the promises in this Agreement, and only in exchange for them, the Company will pay the Employee $84,000, less withholding, in twelve equal monthly installments beginning on the first regular payroll date after this Agreement becomes effective. This payment is consideration to which the Employee is not otherwise entitled.

3. GENERAL RELEASE. The Employee releases the Company and its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns from all claims the Employee has or may have arising on or before the date the Employee signs, including claims under Title VII, the ADA, the ADEA, the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act, the FMLA, the California Fair Employment and Housing Act, the California Labor Code, and the WARN Acts, and all claims in contract and tort.

4. CLAIMS NOT RELEASED. This release does not cover: any claim that cannot be released as a matter of law; a claim for workers' compensation or unemployment benefits; a claim to enforce this Agreement; a claim for indemnification under Labor Code § 2802 or the Company's bylaws; a claim arising after the date the Employee signs; or the Employee's right to file a charge with, or participate in an investigation by, the EEOC, the Civil Rights Department, the NLRB, OSHA, or the SEC. The Employee may not recover monetary relief from any such charge, except that nothing limits the Employee's right to a whistleblower award from the SEC.

5. SECTION 1542 WAIVER. The Employee expressly waives California Civil Code section 1542, which reads: "A GENERAL RELEASE DOES NOT EXTEND TO CLAIMS THAT THE CREDITOR OR RELEASING PARTY DOES NOT KNOW OR SUSPECT TO EXIST IN HIS OR HER FAVOR AT THE TIME OF EXECUTING THE RELEASE AND THAT, IF KNOWN BY HIM OR HER, WOULD HAVE MATERIALLY AFFECTED HIS OR HER SETTLEMENT WITH THE DEBTOR OR RELEASED PARTY." The Employee understands the significance of this waiver and accepts the risk of claims not now known.

6. OWBPA — TIME TO CONSIDER AND REVOKE. Because the Employee is over 40, the release of ADEA claims is governed by 29 U.S.C. § 626(f). The Employee is advised IN WRITING to consult an attorney before signing. The Employee has twenty-one (21) days from receipt to consider this Agreement, and may sign before the period ends but need not. The Employee may revoke the release of ADEA claims within seven (7) days after signing, by written notice to the General Counsel, and this Agreement does not become effective or enforceable until that revocation period expires. If the Employee revokes, the Company owes nothing under Section 2.

7. NO ADMISSION. This Agreement is not an admission of wrongdoing by anyone.

8. CONFIDENTIALITY, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER. The Employee will keep the terms of this Agreement confidential, except to the Employee's spouse, attorney, and tax adviser, or as law requires. Nothing in this Agreement prevents the Employee from discussing or disclosing conduct the Employee reasonably believes to be unlawful, including harassment, discrimination, or retaliation, as California Code of Civil Procedure § 1001 and Government Code § 12964.5 provide, and any provision that purported to do so would be void.

9. NO NON-DISPARAGEMENT OF PROTECTED CONDUCT. The Employee agrees not to disparage the Company, except that this does not limit the Employee's right to disclose information about unlawful acts in the workplace, and the Company acknowledges that a broader clause would be unenforceable under Government Code § 12964.5(b)(1).

10. RETURN OF PROPERTY. The Employee will return all Company property and information by the Separation Date.

11. NO RE-EMPLOYMENT. The Employee agrees not to seek re-employment with the Company, and the Company may decline any application without liability. This does not affect the Employee's rights under Section 4.

12. GOVERNING LAW. California law governs.

13. ENTIRE AGREEMENT. This Agreement is the entire agreement of the parties on its subject and may be amended only in a writing signed by both.

THE EMPLOYEE HAS READ THIS AGREEMENT, UNDERSTANDS IT, AND SIGNS IT VOLUNTARILY.

HALBROOK DIAGNOSTICS, INC.                EMPLOYEE

By: /s/ Marisol Trent                     /s/ Rosalind Achebe Kwan
Name: Marisol Trent                       Rosalind Achebe Kwan
Title: General Counsel                    Date signed: April 14, 2026
